meta.description: Artisan Talents (Handwerks-Talente) from TDE 4.1. These talents represent trade skills and crafts. Tests are normally rolled openly; contested tests are rare. Remaining TP (open test points) are the decisive criterion for quality of created items, treatments, etc. Advancement column B. Encumbrance from armor or backpack can matter for dexterity-heavy crafts.

talents.name: Alchemy
talents.description: This talent governs the creation of 'normal' chemicals and wonder-working potions and mixtures. The player tells the Highlord which alchemical brew the hero wants to make; the Highlord determines difficulty increases or decreases. The hero must have all necessary materials and the recipe. A failed test can have multiple consequences: a harmless but foul-smelling green cloud, or an explosion leveling a city block. Tests can also be used to analyze unknown potions, but a failed test may be disastrous (Highlord should roll secretly). Requires Calculate 4, Read/Write 4, and access to a laboratory (or at minimum a portable analysis kit).

talents.name: Train Animals
talents.description: Whenever a hero wants to teach their animal a trick — a horse the 'silent alarm', a dog to fetch or stand on hind legs — an Animal Training test is required. Difficulty increases come from failed previous attempts (+2 per failed test), the difficulty of the trick, and the animal's basic trainability and potential loyalty. Exercises that are physically or mentally impossible for an animal cannot be taught even by a master trainer. Requires Animal Lore 4 to advance beyond TP 10.

talents.name: Blacksmith
talents.description: Blacksmiths (who also work in brass and bronze) are primarily concerned with creating agricultural tools, shoeing horses, and producing small metal items like nails, bolts, chains, and hinges. They can also repair weapons. Weaponsmiths specialize in metal weapons (create, repair, appraise). Armorers specialize in metal armor (harnesses, lamellas, chain mail). Tinsmiths work with metal sheets and tubes (riveting, soldering; also repair armor). Repairing dented metal armor requires a test with difficulty equal to the armor's AR (15 min/AR point); smoothing a blade notch and reducing BF require separate tests.

talents.name: Boats
talents.description: All talents used for propelling small watercraft — rowing, sailing, paddling, punting — are summarized here. The Highlord should allow heroes to row across a still pond without a test — somehow they will reach the other bank. Sailing, whitewater canoeing, and similar feats require successful tests. Handling larger sailing or rowing vessels requires the Seafaring talent and a larger crew.

talents.name: Bowyer
talents.description: Bowyers and crossbow builders craft missile weapons of all kinds and are the only specialists able to make tension-based projectile weapons. They can also appraise the value of such weapons. Creating a bow or crossbow requires multiple tests (see table); each test takes half a day; a failed test can be salvaged with a double-difficulty test, but a second failure ruins the weapon. Creating arrows/bolts also requires Bowyer tests. Requires Woodcraft 4. Shortbow: 4 tests; Longbow: 6 tests (+1); Warbow: 7 tests (2 tests +3); Light Crossbow: 4 tests (+0); Heavy Crossbow: 12 tests (2 tests +1).

talents.name: Butcher
talents.description: A butcher/slaughterer knows how to humanely kill livestock, extract as many usable materials as possible, and create durable hams, sausages, and roast cuts. Can assess how long meat remains edible and its market price. Similar to an anatomist, knows vulnerable points and causes 1 additional TP in unarmed combat against animals resembling their usual slaughter animals (with Butcher TP 10+). Note: Butcher and Anatomy bonuses do not stack.

talents.name: Cartography
talents.description: A cartographer creates maps and plans, both of buildings and landscapes. During play, successful use means Orientation tests are made easier when the hero is in a tract of nature or cave system they have already explored and mapped. The hero gets useful hints from the Highlord on correctly recording cave systems, buildings, etc. and can better estimate travel distances. Trying to read maps without this talent is confusing and may lead to misinterpretations. Requires Paint/Draw 4.

talents.name: Cheat
talents.description: Depending on test success, the hero may multiply money at stake in a game of chance, or alter dice rolls, exchange cards, etc. A failed test can put the hero in great difficulty. Infamous cheaters have extremely short life expectancies in Aventuria. A high Cheat TP can actually help in a subsequent Perception test to detect others cheating. Wrongly accusing someone of cheating may be grounds for a duel! Tests may be rolled secretly by the Highlord. Requires Human Nature 4.

talents.name: Cook
talents.description: A hero who wants to impress guests (at home or by the campfire) with a delightful meal must pass a successful test, possibly with difficulty increases for complex meals. A barely passed test means edible food was prepared. At least 3 remaining TP after the test: actually tasty. At least 6 remaining TP: culinary delight. In noble courts this art is further specialized — experts for sweet pastries or gravies are not unusual.

talents.name: Drive
talents.description: The type of vehicle and especially the number of draft animals determine the difficulty of a test. Keeping a four-horse racing carriage on the road at low speed requires +4; a cart drawn by a patient mule is much easier. Hazardous maneuvers (passing a city gate at full gallop, halting a runaway brewery cart drawn by six panicking oxen) incur difficulty increases. Steering unfamiliar vehicles (e.g., dog sleds for those used only to horse carriages) is also harder.

talents.name: Farming
talents.description: Basic knowledge of soil conditions, sowing and harvesting, field cultivation, and storage methods. Can identify useful plants and edible crops — thus enabling a shipwrecked group on a deserted island to avoid starvation. Also assesses the value and quality of foodstuffs. Knows how to use a plow, rake, and threshing flail.

talents.name: Leathercraft
talents.description: Covers a wide range of leather working tasks including footwear repair, saddle making, leather clothing, upholstery, and leather armor. Cobblers and saddlers are especially trained in shoes and saddles. Cobblers are the only craftsmen who can fully restore damaged leather armor (not just provisionally patch it). A hero with TP 0 who tries to repair their own shoes will regret the decision on their next march.

talents.name: Light Engineering
talents.description: Based on goldsmithing and fine metalwork, enabling creation of jewelry and filigree works from gold, silver, moonsilver, and other precious metals. Light Engineers can appraise jewelry value. Further applications: engravings in metals, casting small forms (seal matrices, counterfeiting), and assembling mechanisms — clocks, tiny locks, miniature crossbow triggers, or musical clocks. Light Engineers often work closely with stonecutters and jewelers, and frequently are experts in those skills too. Requires Paint/Draw 4.

talents.name: Mining
talents.description: Covers professional digging of tunnels and shafts and their ventilation and drainage. Also enables assessment of underground structures: which beings built them? Where were structural changes made? These questions must be answered by the Highlord after a successful Mining test. It is no surprise that most Aventurian dwarfs understand these matters instinctively. Requires Stone Lore 4 to advance beyond TP 10.

talents.name: Paint/Draw
talents.description: Naturally, anything at the game table can be drawn by players in reality, but in the interest of game flow, talent tests are used. A hero interested in luxury can consider raising this value and earning their bread as a court painter. When encountering primitive tribes, a talented adventurer has already prolonged their life considerably by flattering portraits of the chieftain — and acquired (an unjustified) reputation as a powerful wizard. Remaining TP count for artistic impression of wooden sculptures and similar works.

talents.name: Play Instrument
talents.description: A successful Play Instrument test can earn a few ducats at a prince's court, secure lodging in an inn, but also calm an enraged bear. A hero can specialize in one instrument or try to master several. To produce an even remotely audible performance, at least a barely successful test is needed; to actually earn money, at least 4 remaining TP are recommended.

talents.name: Pick Locks
talents.description: The foundation of the burglar trade. Opening a lock without the right key (using lockpicks, hairpins, knives, etc.) may require tests with significant difficulty increases depending on the lock's quality and construction. A failed test usually means the lockpick or improvised tool broke in the lock, and further opening attempts can only be made under even worse conditions. This talent can also be used to disarm certain types of mechanical traps — but here a failed test always means the trap has been triggered and the hero suffers its full effect. A hero without this talent must pass a DE test at +10 minimum; improvised tools ease by 1, proper lockpicks by 2.

talents.name: Boats
talents.description: Smaller watercraft can be handled with the Boats talent. Seafarers are the only ones who can operate and maintain multi-masted ships. Their duties include setting rigging, taking soundings, maintaining steering gear, supervising cargo, sealing minor leaks, and properly coiling ropes and chains.

talents.name: Stonecutter/Jeweler
talents.description: These professions involve cutting, grinding, polishing, and setting gemstones and crystals of all kinds, primarily for jewelry but also for magical purposes. Requires Stone Lore 4 to advance beyond TP 10.

talents.name: Stonemason
talents.description: A stonemason can create sculptures from stone, carve in high or bas relief, assess different stone types for artistic work, and with a successful test determine the safety of a building or stone bridge (but not tunnels or shafts) and identify what building materials a structure consists of and how much stone and mortar would be needed to erect a particular building. Requires Stone Lore 4.

talents.name: Tailor
talents.description: The Tailor talent primarily covers mending such as sewing on buttons and ribbons, patching, and darning. Higher TP enables alterations to unwanted garments or creating new clothing from scratch. A professional tailor creates garments from fabrics of all kinds — they can create true masterworks from plain cloth. Can assess the value and quality of clothing, repair worn garments to an acceptable condition.

talents.name: Tanner/Furrier
talents.description: This talent serves to make the skin or fur of animals durable and presentable, and to further process it into leather goods or furs — often a rather unpleasant affair requiring a strong stomach and a kind of intuitive alchemy. Tanners and furriers can assess the value and quality of leather and fur goods. An occasionally practiced specialization is the preparation of animal trophies.

talents.name: Tattooing
talents.description: Decorating the skin with images is especially popular among the Thorwalians, who have spread this art to the harbor cities of Aventuria. A tattooist must know where best to place a motif, how much dye to use for different skin types, and must be able to handle a tattooing needle. Tattooists are the only ones who can create permanent skin images. Requires Paint/Draw 4.

talents.name: Treat Disease
talents.description: All types of illness — including dangerous wound fever — can be treated with this talent. The healer first rolls a Recognition test (possibly harder for insidious illnesses) to diagnose and determine required salves or medicines. Then a Healing test (difficulty = illness severity) attempts to initiate recovery, restoring TP equal to remaining talent points. Follow-up tests are possible daily. Failed recognition means no healing; failed healing or follow-up causes 1d6 additional damage. Each test takes different times: recognition 1 round, healing 6 rounds minimum, follow-up 6 rounds minimum (24 hours after healing).

talents.name: Treat Poison
talents.description: A successful Recognition test (possibly harder by half the poison's level for especially insidious poisons) identifies the poison. The Highlord names the poison type and explains how the poisoning must be treated — the healer may first need to gather certain herbs or other ingredients. With prerequisites met, the healer can roll a Treatment test (difficulty = full poison level) to stop the poison's effect and restore TP equal to remaining points. A Follow-up test (possible once, 12 hours later) can restore additional TP. Failed tests have serious consequences (1d6 DP). Each test requires different time: recognition 5 combat rounds minimum, treatment 1 GT minimum, follow-up 1 GT minimum.

talents.name: Treat Wounds
talents.description: Fractures, cuts, stabs, and other combat or accident injuries are treated with this talent. First Aid: a critically injured hero (0 or fewer VP) can be saved by a successful test, harder by twice the negative VP count; takes twice as many combat rounds as VP below 0, minus remaining TP after test. If failed, patient suffers 1d6 additional damage. On success, patient has exactly 1 VP. Wound Healing: first test (general wound care; prevents wound fever), second test to initiate healing (difficulty +3 per wound); remaining TP after second test ease the patient's CN check for natural healing. Failed tests or fumbles cause 1d6 additional damage or stop healing for 24 hours.

talents.name: Woodcraft
talents.description: This talent has many applications in daily hero life: replacing a rotten boat plank, creating an improvised weapon or tool, quickly whittling a children's toy. A successful test can mean the successful creation or repair of a wooden item. For completing complex wooden devices or especially artful carvings, a difficulty increase should apply. Remaining TP are counted for the artistic impression of wooden sculptures. Note: Bowyer requires Woodcraft 4; Carpenter requires Woodcraft 4.

talents.name: Carpenter
talents.description: Carpenters, ship carpenters, and roofers master various types of woodworking but (in contrast to standard Woodcraft) deal with larger wooden projects such as stairs, roof beams, or ship masts — their statics and joints. Also capable of assessing the value and structural integrity of wooden constructions. Requires Woodcraft 4 to advance beyond TP 10.
